findings.where: research/blueprint/restructure/RS-21.result.json: SR.5 kept scope; owner 'Nonarchimedean derivatives, integral co-Whittaker families and their local center action'; SR.5 -> AutomorphicCongruences:L3; compare R16.2
findings.claim: The L3 import is assigned to SR.5 without an essential-vector supplier theorem. SR.5 retains derivatives, co-Whittaker families and center/projective interpolation, not conductor-level invariant lines and coefficient specialization. R16.2 retains the local GL2 conductor/newvector theorem, but neither its scope nor the owner/export records provide the integral family comparison this consumer needs. Derivative base change and characteristic-zero newvector dimensions alone do not supply invariant-line base change.
findings.evidence: At audit commit 5e3762c44fbdaf9f40e434f7f11dc809769dcdc4, AutomorphicCongruences L3 says 'derivatives/co-Whittaker/essential vectors from SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups' and requires FW Appendix A compatibility; SR.5 names no essential-vector theorem and its L3 link describes only derivatives/co-Whittaker families. Fouquet-Wan https://arxiv.org/pdf/2107.13726v3, Appendix A section 6.2, Propositions 6.8-6.9, printed pp.77-78, read 2026-10-01: invariant modules are 'free of rank 1' and their natural specialization map is an isomorphism, at the conductor-level subgroup under the preceding coefficient and unchanged-monodromy hypotheses. This is not the top-derivative base-change theorem.
findings.fix: Assign the coefficient-qualified integral essential-vector/invariant-line comparison to the canonical smooth-local family plan and add its precise export to L3. Preserve R16.2 as owner of the field-valued GL2 newvector case; when reusing it, put the integral comparison in a later distinct substage consuming SR.5 and R16.2, not a reverse R16.2 -> SR.5 link, which would cycle. Transcribe/reconcile the source coefficient setting and minimal-monodromy restrictions; do not assert arbitrary invariant base change. Add requests or declaration-level nodes, the invariant-line map API and specialization tests in the owning blueprint, not theorem copies in L3 or edits to atlas base files.

findings.where: research/blueprint/restructure/RS-21.result.json: R16.5 keeps/reason; AL.3 -> R16.5 link; global-expansion owner ledger
findings.claim: The proposal treats the global GL2 Whittaker expansion as new retained R16.5 work, while importing general GL_n x GL_m cuspidal global unfolding from AL.3 without assigning the general Fourier-Whittaker expansion prerequisite an explicit owner or recording the general/special comparison. Local SR.5 functors do not construct the global adelic expansion. If AL.3 implicitly includes the general theorem, the GL2 case must be reuse/comparison; otherwise the general-rank proof has a missing supplier. The ownership boundary leaves these alternatives unresolved.
findings.evidence: At audit commit 5e3762c44fbdaf9f40e434f7f11dc809769dcdc4, R16.5 retains 'GL₂ global Whittaker expansion' and says 'the global expansion and converse theorem remain new'. AL.3 promises 'the global unfolding for cuspidal data' for GL_n x GL_m, but no proposal owner covers the general expansion. Cogdell https://people.math.osu.edu/cogdell.1/pcmi-www.pdf, L-functions and Converse Theorems for GL_n, section 1.1 Theorem 1.1, printed p.7, and section 2.2.2, printed pp.20-21, read 2026-10-01: the general adelic expansion has 'convergence absolute and uniform on compact subsets'; unfolding substitutes a Fourier expansion before justified summation/integration interchange. The retained n=2 construction does not supply arbitrary n.
findings.fix: Name one owner for the general cuspidal GL_n adelic Fourier-Whittaker expansion and convergence/interchange API, naturally a lower AL.3 component or canonical global automorphic component feeding AL.3. SR.5 retains only its nonarchimedean local functors. Make R16.5's GL2 work a comparison/application to integral models and classical normalization, retaining its distinct converse theorem. Record the owner/export in the proposal and route declaration-level nodes or requests into its owner's blueprint. Use AL.3 -> R16.5; do not add the reverse edge, which would cycle.
